jobs.title: Manager, Provider Recruitment
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Us:

Grow was born to tackle a critical challenge: making mental health care more effective and accessible for everyone. Since launching in 2020, 15 million sessions have started on Grow, and we've barely scratched the surface. We do it through a three-sided marketplace that empowers providers, augments insurance payors, and serves patients. Every solution we build reveals ten more waiting to be delivered, and that's just what gets us going. We've backed that ambition with more than $328M in funding, including our Series D at a $3B valuation from Sequoia Capital, Transformation Capital, TCV, SignalFire, Menlo Ventures, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, and others.

At Grow, the work you do can literally change someone's life. Your work here doesn't stay on a screen; it impacts whether someone can find, afford, and access quality care. That ambition sets us apart, and offers you an endless runway to impact one of the world's most urgent issues. We don’t have passenger seats here. Everyone is driving something that matters.

This work deserves real commitment. So if you thrive on meeting problems head on, untangling serious complexity, and working at pace with the sharpest yet kindest people around, you've come to the right place.

The Opportunity:

We are looking for a Provider Recruitment Manager to help us scale our PGA model, primarily focused on our Inbound motion. You'll manage a pod of 8+ Provider Growth Associates (PGAs), coaching them to convert interested providers into engaged, active members of our network. You'll be part of a team of 30+ PGAs organized across manager pods, reporting directly to the Director of Provider Recruitment.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Manage a team of 8+ PGAs, running weekly metrics-driven 1:1s and hands-on coaching and training to develop skills and close performance gaps

  • Hold a high performance bar for your team - proactively identify areas of opportunity for improvement, both within your team and across the broader department

  • Support org-wide communications, serving as a critical layer in communicating change and driving implementation across the team

  • Lead organization-wide strategic projects that impact the broader Recruitment org (AI enablement, workflow redesigns, communication improvements)

  • Build connection and engagement across a fully remote team - creating rhythms and touch points that keep your team aligned, motivated, and collaborative despite the distance

You’ll Be a Good Fit If You:

  • Proven leadership experience - you have 1+ years of experience managing and developing a high-performing recruitment, sales development, or transactional sales team, backed by 5+ overall years in a recruitment, sales, or client-facing function

  • Move with urgency without cutting corners - you're responsive, decisive and move fast rather than chasing perfect, but you never sacrifice the small details that matter; balancing both is what separates good from great

  • Data-driven, AI-fluent - you bring data to the table to tell a story, not just report numbers, rooting decisions in fact over feeling; you actively use AI to analyze data, orchestrate workflows, and spot coaching opportunities in your team's calls and metrics, working smarter and more efficiently every day

  • Think creatively and stay open-minded - you don't assume the way you did it before is the way to do it here; you bring strong opinions but hold them loosely and collaborate to find what actually works

  • Get in the trenches with your team - you'll jump on calls, help draft emails, get deep into systems, and roll up your sleeves alongside your PGAs every day, not just coach from the sidelines

  • Lead with empathy - you genuinely care about your team members as people, not just as numbers on a dashboard

Employment Type: Fulltime, Exempt
Base Compensation: The annual compensation for this role is:

Fully Remote Commitment: $114,000-$136,000 base salary + up to $20,000 in variable compensation

This role is fully remote. Both arrangements include travel 2–3 times per year (e.g., company and department offsites).

If you don’t meet every single requirement, but are still interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box, and Grow believes the perfect candidate is more than just a resume.

Full Time Employee Benefits:

  • Health Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life, and disability coverage.

  • Grow for Grow: No cost access to therapy through the Grow platform (available to US employees)

  • Financial Wellness: Retirement savings programs and equity opportunities to help you invest in your future.

  • Flexible Time Off, Paid Holidays & Winter Break: Flexible time off, company paid holidays (which vary by country), and a full company wide Winter Break to rest and recharge

  • Parental Leave: Up to 18 weeks of paid parental leave to support you and your growing family and a new child stipend.

  • Mental Health Mornings/Afternoons: Dedicated weekly flexible time for self care, whether that's therapy, exercise, journaling, time with family, or simply taking a break.

  • Wellness & Development Stipend: Annual stipend to support your personal wellbeing and professional growth, from fitness and education to books and learning resources.

  • Commuter Benefits: Pre tax commuter benefits to support teammates working from one of our hub locations.

  • Home Office & Meals: Support for your home workspace plus meal benefits, with offerings tailored to both remote and hub based employees.

  • Additional Perks: A variety of wellbeing benefits, including wellness memberships, virtual care, pet insurance discounts (where available), and global travel assistance.


Research shows that some groups hesitate to apply unless they meet every qualification. If you’re excited about this role but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply. At Grow, we value diverse experiences, transferable skills, and the unique strengths each person brings.

Grow Therapy is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.

Use of AI Tools: We use certain AI and automated tools to support recruitment. These tools help our team review applications, organize interviews, detect potential application integrity issues, and maintain interview records; they do not make final hiring decisions.

Application Review: Ashby's AI-Assisted Application Review helps review application materials against role-specific criteria and may flag potential fraud or integrity issues for recruiter review. All advancement decisions are made by our human recruiting team after independent review. See Ashby's AI Bias Audit Report.

Interview Recording: We use BrightHire to record interviews, supporting note-taking and consistency across candidates. Learn more. Interviews are confidential; you may ask your interviewer to stop recording anytime, or opt out in advance. Choosing not to be recorded will not, by itself, affect your candidacy.

AI-Assisted Recruiter Screen: For select roles, BrightHire's AI features may help structure initial recruiter screens and organize interview notes. All responses are reviewed by our recruiting team; no hiring decisions are made by AI alone.

State-specific notices: Depending on your location, you may have additional rights. Illinois: If AI analyzes a video interview, we'll provide notice, explain how it works and what it evaluates, and obtain consent beforehand. New York City: Where required, we'll provide at least 10 business days’ notice before using an automated employment decision tool and explain how to request an alternative process. Maryland: We do not use facial recognition to create facial templates during interviews unless required notice and written consent are obtained.

Questions, accommodation requests, requests for an alternative selection process, objections to recording, or concerns about AI use? Contact talentops@growtherapy.com. We’re happy to help or offer an alternative way to participate.

The Opportunity:

We're looking for a Senior or Staff Product Designer to join our Product Growth team. This role will shape how clients discover and navigate early parts of their experience with Grow Therapy. The Product Growth team is within our Match Success org, one of Grow's highest-priority areas where we help clients identify their needs, evaluate potential providers, and get them started on their therapy journey. You'll lead 0→1 design work — from strategy through launch — impacting millions of people looking for mental health support, and set the craft bar for how growth-focused design gets done at Grow. You’ll stand out as an applicant if you’ve worked on a consumer-focused growth team (B2C).

What You'll Be Doing:

  • Explore a wide array of hypotheses and problems and then strive to create a clear point of view on what to build, translating business goals and client needs into concrete design briefs and roadmap milestones

  • Bring clarity to ambiguous, cross-team growth problems — funnel drop-off, activation friction, new programs, channel optimizations — and turn them into shippable design work

  • Design and prototype end-to-end, from early concept through high-fidelity design and production handoff, staying close through iteration to resolve issues as they arise

  • Champion design excellence by treating product as an extension of of our brand, ensuring every touchpoint meets the highest quality standards

  • Partner with Product Management, Data Science, and Engineering to design and interpret experiments, using quantitative and qualitative signals to inform design decisions

  • Use AI-powered tools as a natural part of your workflow to prototype faster, explore more directions, and multiply your own and your team's output without sacrificing craft

You'll Be a Good Fit If:

  • 6+ years of end-to-end (UX and UI) product design experience on consumer-facing or marketplace products; growth team experience a plus, consumer-grade quality a must

  • Portfolio demonstrating craft excellence, systems thinking, and leadership through influence on consumer experiences —shipped outcomes, not just polished mocks

  • Strong visual design sensibility, with range across systemized UI and more expressive, brand-forward work

  • Experience leading design on high-impact projects, including giving direction and feedback to other designers

  • Ability to think strategically about product vision — not just how something should look, but what should be built and why

  • Experience shipping applications or software across mobile and web

  • Skilled at using AI as a creative and productivity multiplier, moving faster and exploring more ideas without sacrificing judgment

  • Excellent communication skills, able to articulate and defend design decisions to both design and non-design partners

  • Experience establishing design workflows, systems, and team practices that scale beyond a single project

  • Proven ability to collaborate effectively with Engineering, PM, and other disciplines as true partners, not just stakeholders

Employment Type: Full Time

This is a hybrid role with the expectation to work onsite from our NYC or SF hub location three days per week (Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday) and travel 2–3 times per year (ex. team workshops, hackathons, company and department offsites).

The base compensation for this role will vary depending on several factors, including relevant experience, qualifications, and the candidate's working location.

Role Details:

Employment Type: Full Time, Exempt
Base Compensation: The base compensation range for this position is:

  • Hybrid Commitment: $182,000 - 227,000 USD Annually

This role is hybrid (onsite from our NYC, San Francisco, or Seattle hub location three days per week: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday). Expect to travel 2–3 times per year (e.g., company and department offsites).

The base compensation for this role will vary depending on several factors, including relevant experience, qualifications, and the candidate’s working location.

  • Wellness & Development Stipend: Annual stipend to support your personal wellbeing and professional growth, from fitness and education to books and learning resources.

  • Home Office & Meals: Support for your home workspace plus meal benefits, with offerings tailored to both remote and hub based employees.

This work deserves real commitment. So if you thrive on meeting problems head on, untangling serious complexity, and working at pace with the sharpest yet kindest people around, you've come to the right place.

The Opportunity

We're hiring a Software Engineer to help build and evolve the backend systems that power Grow Therapy's platform. In this role, you'll design, implement, and ship server-side features and services that directly impact how clients and providers connect, communicate, and access care.

You'll join a collaborative, product-focused engineering organization where technical work is closely tied to reliability, scalability, and real-world outcomes. This role is ideal for an engineer who takes pride in writing clean, well-tested code, thinks carefully about system design and data integrity, and is energized by the opportunity to grow alongside a fast-moving team.

Why This Role Matters

Access to mental healthcare in America is still deeply fragmented and Grow Therapy is building the platform to fix that. This work deserves real commitment. So if you thrive on meeting problems head on, untangling serious complexity, and working at pace with the sharpest yet kindest people around, you've come to the right place.

The Opportunity

Grow Therapy works with most of the largest health plans in the country. As those relationships have matured, the interesting question has shifted from whether a plan works with us to what we should build together, and there is no standard answer to that question.

This role owns a focused set of key relationships end to end. You decide what should be built with each plan, design the structure that delivers it, negotiate it, and stay with it once it is live.

The work runs on a multi-year horizon. You will spend real time with health plans’ senior executives, enough that they bring you problems before they have decided what to do about them.

You will work closely with our Director, Payor Strategy and our VP, Corporate and Business Development on a team small enough that each person carries a meaningful share of the company's strategy and influence to drive it.

What You'll Be Doing

Deciding what to build

  • Develop a point of view on each health plan you cover: where their behavioral health strategy is heading, what is not working, who owns the problem internally, and what would need to be true for them to commit to something ambitious.

About the Role

We’re hiring a Senior Platform Reliability Engineer to help define and scale reliability as a first-class capability at Grow. In this role you’ll operate horizontally across the organization, shaping how reliability is understood, measured, and built into the developer experience.

You’ll work closely with other members of the platform team as well as our product engineering teams to establish standards around observability, SLOs/SLAs, and incident response—while also helping translate those standards into self-service tooling and “golden paths” that make it easy for teams to adopt them.

This is a high-impact, highly autonomous role where you’ll drive both cultural and technical change, ultimately enabling teams to independently build and operate reliable systems at scale.

What You'll Work On

You’ll help us establish and scale reliability as a discipline at Grow by:

  • Defining Reliability Standards Establishing frameworks for SLOs/SLAs, error budgets, and operational readiness; helping teams understand what to measure and why it matters.

  • Improving Observability & Measurement Identifying gaps in metrics, logging, and tracing; ensuring services are measurable, debuggable, and aligned with reliability goals.

  • Evolving Incident Response Developing and improving incident response practices, from detection to post-incident learning, and helping teams build sustainable on-call and escalation patterns.

  • Enabling Self-Service Reliability Partnering with the platform team to build tooling and abstractions (e.g., service scorecards, dashboards, templates, golden paths) that make it easy for teams to adopt and stay compliant with reliability standards.

  • Driving Adoption Across Teams Working cross-functionally to educate, influence, and guide engineering teams—scaling reliability practices through a combination of clear standards, strong communication, and developer-friendly systems

Who You Are

  • Experienced in production systems: You have 6+ years of experience operating and improving reliability of production systems at scale.

  • Strong foundation in cloud and infrastructure: You have hands-on experience with AWS, Kubernetes (e.g., EKS), and infrastructure as code tools like Terraform.

  • Deep understanding of reliability principles: You’ve defined or worked with SLOs/SLAs, understand error budgets, and have experience improving reliability through measurement and iteration.

  • Observability expertise: You’ve worked with modern observability tooling (we use DataDog) and understand how to build actionable monitoring systems across metrics, logs, and traces.

  • Systems thinker: You’re able to zoom out, identify patterns across teams and services, and design solutions that scale beyond a single system.

  • Impact-oriented: You focus on outcomes over output and care deeply about improving real reliability outcomes—not just adding processes.

  • Strong communicator and influencer: You can drive change across teams without direct authority, balancing pragmatism with long-term vision.

  • Self-directed: You thrive in ambiguous environments and are comfortable defining problems, proposing solutions, and executing independently.

  • Team player: You collaborate well, communicate with empathy, and enjoy mentoring and learning from others.

Bonus Points

  • You’ve helped introduce or scale reliability practices in a growing organization.

  • You’ve built internal tooling or platforms used by multiple teams.

  • You have experience designing service-level scorecards or compliance/reporting systems.

  • You’ve worked with both SaaS (e.g., DataDog) and self-managed observability stacks.

  • You were previously a product engineer and bring empathy for developer experience.

  • You have experience with database reliability and performance (we use PostgreSQL)

Why This Role Is Exciting

This is a rare opportunity to define what reliability looks like at a growing, scaling engineering organization—and to do it in a way that actually sticks.

You won’t just be responding to incidents or working within a single team. You’ll be shaping how reliability is measured, enforced, and experienced across the entire company. You’ll work alongside your team mates to turn best practices into intuitive, self-service systems that engineers rely on every day.

Your work will directly improve system reliability, reduce incidents, and enable teams to move faster with confidence, ultimately making reliability a built-in property of how we build software at Grow.

Role Details

  • Employment Type: Full Time, Exempt

  • Base Compensation: The base compensation range for this position is $182,000–$250,000 USD Annually.

This is a hybrid role with the expectation to work onsite from our San Francisco, NYC, or Seattle hub location three days per week (Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday) and travel 2–3 times per year (e.g., company and department offsites).

The base compensation for this role will vary depending on several factors, including relevant experience, qualifications, and the candidate’s working location.

  • Health Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life, and disability coverage.

  • Grow for Grow: No cost access to therapy through the Grow platform (available to US employees)

  • Financial Wellness: Retirement savings programs and equity opportunities to help you invest in your future.

  • Flexible Time Off, Paid Holidays & Winter Break: Flexible time off, company paid holidays (which vary by country), and a full company wide Winter Break to rest and recharge

  • Parental Leave: Up to 18 weeks of paid parental leave to support you and your growing family and a new child stipend.

  • Mental Health Mornings/Afternoons: Dedicated weekly flexible time for self care, whether that's therapy, exercise, journaling, time with family, or simply taking a break.

  • Wellness & Development Stipend: Annual stipend to support your personal wellbeing and professional growth, from fitness and education to books and learning resources.

  • Commuter Benefits: Pre tax commuter benefits to support teammates working from one of our hub locations.

  • Home Office & Meals: Support for your home workspace plus meal benefits, with offerings tailored to both remote and hub based employees.

  • Additional Perks: A variety of wellbeing benefits, including wellness memberships, virtual care, pet insurance discounts (where available), and global travel assistance.

The Opportunity

This is a Senior or Staff level role owning detection and incident response at Grow. The core of the job is: catching threats early through strong detection engineering, moving fast on unfamiliar systems when something does happen, and having a real point of view on where the architecture is exposed before it becomes a problem. It's cross functional by design, working closely with infrastructure, engineering, and compliance.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Share security judgment and standards with teams across the company, raising the bar beyond the security org itself

  • Investigate and resolve security incidents across endpoint, network, and cloud, understanding unfamiliar systems well enough to respond with confidence

  • Research the threats and attack methods most relevant to a healthcare marketplace, and use that intelligence to get ahead of them

  • Build and mature Grow's detection and response program, and participate in an incident on call rotation

  • Strengthen our cloud security posture in partnership with infrastructure, engineering, and compliance

  • Build defense in depth through secure by default architecture and processes, thinking through the full lifecycle of a problem rather than just patching the immediate risk

  • Design new, creative approaches to catching threats early, not just tuning what already exists

You'll Be a Good Fit If

  • You have 6+ years of experience in detection and incident response

  • You have real depth in AWS security: IAM, secure service configuration, CloudTrail, SCPs, AWS Organizations, Config, and the like

  • You have deep expertise responding to complex incidents and a strong grasp of detection engineering, including SIEM, EDR, and CSPM tooling

  • You care about how security work lands on the people around you, from customers whose data you protect to the engineers you partner with

  • You write code to automate the tedious parts of the job, and you're comfortable with infrastructure as code

  • You collaborate well, both within a security team and across engineering more broadly

  • You think about the whole solution, not just the technology, and can weigh competing design choices with real conviction

  • You understand the current threat landscape and know how to assess risk against it

  • Making our large codebase fast to work in: build systems and monorepo tooling, CI/CD pipeline performance, test reliability and framework strategy

  • Drive the technical strategy for breaking up the monolith, from the incremental migration path to the test-isolation and build tooling that makes it possible at scale.

  • Embedding with product teams to understand their workflows firsthand, and treating their feedback as product input

  • Raising the bar for the engineers around you through design review, mentorship, and the quality of your own shipped work

  • You think about developer tools with a product mindset, defining what success looks like up front and measuring adoption and developer satisfaction to know you've delivered it.

  • You think about developer tools with a product mindset, measuring adoption and developer satisfaction rather than shipping and hoping

  • You are genuinely excited about AI development tooling and have opinions grounded in things you have built

  • Bonus: Python ecosystem depth, GitHub Actions at scale, or prior experience driving standards across a 100+ engineer organization

  • Bonus: you've built developer-facing AI tooling - coding agents, AI code review, LLM developer workflows, MCP - and have a grounded view of where it does and doesn't help.

You'll also be in a rare position to shape how AI gets used in security here, not just adopting tools yourself, but designing agents that take on real security work.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Design and build the security foundation for Grow's infrastructure as it scales

  • Research the threats and attack methods most relevant to Grow's applications and infrastructure, and turn that research into real solutions

  • Improve our cloud security posture in close partnership with infrastructure, engineering, and compliance

  • Respond to security incidents, from critical to routine, and participate in an on call rotation

  • Build defense in depth through secure by default architecture, closing gaps before they turn into incidents

  • Define and track the KPIs that show whether our cloud security program is actually working

  • Build and deploy AI agents that strengthen threat detection, alert triage, vulnerability management, and incident response, reasoning through problems and escalating to a human when needed


You'll Be a Good Fit If

  • 6+ years of experience in the Cloud Security domain.

  • You have deep AWS security experience: IAM, secure service configuration, CloudTrail, SCPs, AWS Organizations, Config, and similar tooling

  • You have real depth in Kubernetes security, including secure deployments, network policies, service to service auth, RBAC, workload identity, admission controllers, and runtime security

  • You're comfortable with infrastructure as code and think about the full lifecycle of a problem, not just the tool that patches it

  • You care about how your work lands on the people around you, from the patients whose data you protect to the teams you partner with, and you bring strong opinions to security design decisions

  • You've actually built and deployed production grade AI agents or agent powered tools for security work, not just experimented with or advised on them

Employment Type: Full Time, Exempt
Base Compensation: The base compensation range for this position is:

  • Hybrid Commitment: $182,000- $250,000 USD Annually

  • Fully Remote Commitment: $152,000–$208,000 USD Annually

This role can be hybrid (onsite from our NYC, San Francisco, or Seattle hub location three days per week: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday) or fully remote. Both arrangements include travel 2–3 times per year (e.g., company and department offsites).

The base compensation for this role will vary depending on several factors, including relevant experience, qualifications, and the candidate’s working location.

  • Health Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life, and disability coverage.

  • Grow for Grow: No cost access to therapy through the Grow platform (available to US employees)

  • Financial Wellness: Retirement savings programs and equity opportunities to help you invest in your future.

  • Parental Leave: Up to 18 weeks of paid parental leave to support you and your growing family and a new child stipend.

  • Mental Health Mornings/Afternoons: Dedicated weekly flexible time for self care, whether that's therapy, exercise, journaling, time with family, or simply taking a break.

  • Wellness & Development Stipend: Annual stipend to support your personal wellbeing and professional growth, from fitness and education to books and learning resources.

  • Commuter Benefits: Pre tax commuter benefits to support teammates working from one of our hub locations.

  • Home Office & Meals: Support for your home workspace plus meal benefits, with offerings tailored to both remote and hub based employees.

  • Excellent communication and cross-functional leadership.

  • Experience building high-performance teams.

About Us:

Grow was born to tackle a critical challenge: making mental health care more effective and accessible for everyone. Since launching in 2020, 15 million sessions have started on Grow, and we've barely scratched the surface. We do it through a three-sided marketplace that empowers providers, augments insurance payors, and serves patients. Every solution we build reveals ten more waiting to be delivered, and that's just what gets us going. We've backed that ambition with more than $328M in funding, including our Series D at a $3B valuation from Sequoia Capital, Transformation Capital, TCV, SignalFire, Menlo Ventures, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, and others.

At Grow, the work you do can literally change someone's life. Your work here doesn't stay on a screen; it impacts whether someone can find, afford, and access quality care. That ambition sets us apart, and offers you an endless runway to impact one of the world's most urgent issues. We don’t have passenger seats here. Everyone is driving something that matters.

This work deserves real commitment. So if you thrive on meeting problems head on, untangling serious complexity, and working at pace with the sharpest yet kindest people around, you've come to the right place.

We’re looking for a Senior Business Data Analyst, Business Analytics to play a critical role in enabling data-driven decision-making across the organization. You will partner with business leaders to scope, design, and build the appropriate analytical tools and metrics to answer strategic and operational questions. This will include defining and operationalizing key performance indicators (KPIs), uncovering insights through rigorous analysis, developing scalable dashboards and reporting frameworks, and ultimately translating data into business value. Success in this role is measured by the impact of insights on strategic and operational decisions, clarity of metrics delivered, and measurable improvements in business outcomes such as growth, efficiency, and customer satisfaction.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Elicit and synthesize data-driven insights into clear narratives and recommendations that influence decision-making, including recurring business reviews, strategic planning sessions, and ad hoc deep dives.

  • Enable business leaders to make data-driven decisions by translating their business needs into the appropriate analytical tools and metrics to answer strategic and operational questions such as identifying growth levers, diagnosing performance gaps, or evaluating initiative impact.

  • Scope, design, build, and maintain dashboards, reporting tools, and data models to enable self-service access to key metrics and ensure data accuracy, consistency, and accessibility across teams.

  • Use AI tools to accelerate your workflow and increase the quality of your output via querying, modeling, and synthesizing findings. You validate AI-assisted work rather than taking it at face value, and you build with scalability in mind so your solutions hold up as reliable, reusable processes.

You’ll be a good fit if you are:

  • A Problem Solver: You have 3+ years of experience in BI or data analytics at a high-growth tech startup. You’re able to identify business challenges based on metrics and analyses, and you’re ready to recommend solutions to improve business processes. You balance analysis with decisive execution to avoid “analysis paralysis.”

    • Strong bonus: Experience solving data problems in a healthcare-related field (e.g., RCM, provider operations, value-based care, health tech SaaS).

  • A data-driven decision maker: You have expert-level SQL skills and are familiar with tools like Snowflake, DBT, Looker, Hex, and Retool. You spend most of your day building critical analyses and data visualizations to elicit data-driven insights. You use metrics and analyses to uncover insights, validate hypotheses, and guide operational decisions. You are able to dive deep to understand the full scope of data, including edge cases.

  • AI-native: AI tools are part of how you naturally work day-to-day. You default to using AI to speed up querying, drafting, and synthesis, and you know when to lean on it versus when deeper manual analysis is warranted. You stay current on new tools and techniques and bring that thinking back to how the team works.

  • An effective communicator: You are adept at translating complex analytical concepts to non-technical stakeholders. You are comfortable presenting to executives, business leaders, engineers, PMs, and peers. You are expert at crafting compelling data stories through visualizations.

  • Mission-Driven: You’re here to change the world, and you’re always connecting your work back to the importance of the Grow Therapy mission.

  • Agile: You thrive in a fast-paced, unpredictable environment, and you’re able to pivot as new priorities emerge. You are skilled at managing multiple stakeholders, projects, and timelines efficiently.

  • A Team Player: You’re collaborative by nature, relish in camaraderie and group wins, and are looked to by your colleagues as a steadfast partner and source of encouragement.

About the Role

We are looking for a Director of Lifecycle & Retention to lead the delivery of an excellent customer experience across our multi-sided marketplace. In this role, you’ll own retention and lifecycle marketing - accountable for both strategy and execution. You will develop learning agendas, partner on advanced measurement approaches, and ensure that every initiative delivers clear, measurable impact and business growth through excellent experiences.

You will work closely with Product, Engineering, Customer service, Finance, and Creative to build strategies with alignment, accelerate performance outcomes, and bring the right message to the right customer at the right time. You will also oversee our lifecycle team and lead cross-functional initiatives that strengthen our approach to engagement, cohort health, and long-term retention.

The ideal candidate is a seasoned lifecycle and retention leader who is deeply customer obsessed, with strong analytical instincts and a bias for action, fluency across CRM and lifecycle tooling, and a track record of turning insights into scaled, measurable business growth. You are equally versed in how to design marketing programs and in how to influence product decisions through how deeply you learn about customer behavior. You bring structure to complexity and know how to guide teams toward rigor, clarity, and meaningful performance outcomes.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Develop the strategy and roadmap for retention & lifecycle marketing across our customer journeys, spanning onboarding to long term loyalty loops.

  • Create and manage learning agendas and experiment frameworks that validate performance and inform prioritization

  • Build and own retention measurement and data in partnership with Data and Finance, including cohort analysis, LTV modeling, churn prediction, and attribution mapping

  • Own lifecycle channels and messaging systems (email, push, in-app, SMS, and emerging formats), ensuring the right participant is reached with the right message at the right moment

  • Lead and develop a world-class lifecycle and retention org

  • Collaborate deeply with product and engineering teams to inform the roadmap, improve signal quality, and build the tracking and infrastructure that lifecycle programs depend on

  • Partner with Product, Creative, Data, and Finance teams to set shared objectives, align on learning agendas, and drive accountability against measurable business growth

  • Evaluate customer-level and cohort-level insights to guide optimization, product decisions, and resource investment - and ultimately drive improved customer outcomes

  • Lead cross-functional reviews, planning cycles, and post-mortems to ensure the organization has clear visibility into results and is operating strategically

  • Develop scalable systems, documentation, and workflows that support transparency, efficiency, and improved results

  • Stay current with lifecycle trends, measurement standards, and platform capabilities to identify new opportunities for engagement and efficiency

This role is based in our New York, NY hub, where we require an in-office presence three days per week.

You Will Be a Good Fit If You Have

  • 10+ years of experience in lifecycle marketing, retention, or CRM, ideally within a consumer marketplace and/or a high-growth performance-driven organization

  • A proven track record of building and scaling lifecycle programs across multiple audiences that drive measurable business outcomes

  • Demonstrated expertise with cohort analysis, LTV and churn modeling, experimentation, attribution frameworks, and lifecycle and CRM platforms

  • Strong analytical capabilities and the ability to translate data into actionable insights and clear recommendations

  • Experience informing product decisions and partnering closely with product and engineering teams to ship against a shared roadmap

  • A genuine obsession with the customer and a habit of grounding every decision in participant behavior and needs

  • A strategic and operational mindset, with the ability to set long-term direction while executing near-term objectives

  • Exceptional communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills across technical and non-technical teams

  • A steady, proactive, solutions-oriented approach when navigating ambiguity or competing priorities

  • A relentless focus on measurable impact and driving real, durable business growth

Employment Type: Full Time, Exempt
Base Compensation: The base compensation range for this position is:

Hybrid Commitment: $189,000 - $231,000 USD Annually

This role is hybrid (onsite from our NYC hub location three days per week: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday). Arrangements include travel 2–3 times per year (e.g., company and department offsites).

The base compensation for this role will vary depending on several factors, including relevant experience, qualifications, and the candidate’s working location.

You will also lead cross-functional initiatives that strengthen our approach to account targeting, lead quality, funnel health, and sustainable yet rapid growth.

The ideal candidate is a seasoned ABM marketer who has run employer growth in a fast-growing healthcare organization before—scrappy yet strategic, with strong customer instincts and a bias for action, deep fluency in account-based B2B lifecycles, paid channels, landing pages, and full-funnel optimization, and a track record of both 0→1 and 1→many. You are equally versed in how to run efficient, targeted account-based programs at scale and in how to identify and build entirely new growth channels from the ground up. The Opportunity

1 in 4 people need mental health care, and most can't get it. Grow is building the infrastructure to change that, and the teams you help build will directly shape how quickly and how well we can expand access to care. Grow has reached meaningful scale, but we're still early enough that individual talent decisions can materially change our trajectory. You'll lead Business Recruiters who own distinct parts of the company, set the strategy for the function, and partner directly with senior leaders on critical talent and organizational decisions - while staying close enough to the work to personally lead our most important searches. What You’ll Do

  • Lead and develop senior Business Recruiters, setting a high bar for recruiting craft, sourcing, judgment, execution, and business partnership.

  • Partner with senior leaders on talent strategy, org design, profiles, leveling, compensation, and hiring decisions, using data and market insight to shape outcomes.

  • Personally lead select critical and high-impact searches from market definition through close.

  • Evolve key recruiting programs, including referrals, interviewer certification, internal mobility, Bar Raiser expansion, and AI-enabled workflows.

  • Build the team and leadership bench needed to scale, developing senior recruiters into stronger functional owners and future leaders.

What You Bring

  • 12+ years of recruiting experience, with significant experience supporting business or non-technical functions in a fast-moving company.

  • Proven people leadership experience managing experienced recruiters, raising standards, developing talent, and addressing underperformance.

  • Experience leading recruiters who independently own senior stakeholders, business units, or complex hiring portfolios.

  • Deep recruiting craft across search strategy, market mapping, sourcing, assessment, stakeholder management, and closing.

  • A track record of personally leading complex, high-impact, and senior-level searches.

  • Strong data fluency and operating discipline, with the ability to diagnose performance and turn insights into action.

  • Strong executive judgment and influence, including the ability to challenge senior leaders and shape talent strategy.

  • Experience translating business priorities into workforce and recruiting strategies across competing needs.

  • Comfort operating in a high-growth environment that requires both strategic leadership and hands-on execution.

Nice to Have

  • Experience building or scaling recruiting programs beyond core delivery.

  • Experience using modern recruiting technology, including AI, to improve sourcing, decision-making, and team effectiveness.

  • You code well enough to automate tedious work and build frameworks or services that solve real security problems

Grow was born to tackle a critical challenge: making mental health care more effective and accessible for everyone. Since launching in 2020, 15 million sessions have started on Grow, and we've barely scratched the surface. We do it through a three-sided marketplace that empowers providers, augments insurance payors, and serves patients. Every solution we build reveals ten more waiting to be delivered, and that's just what gets us going. We've backed that ambition with more than $328M in funding, including our Series D at a $3B valuation from Sequoia Capital, Transformation Capital, TCV, SignalFire, Menlo Ventures, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, and others.

At Grow, the work you do can literally change someone's life. Your work here doesn't stay on a screen; it impacts whether someone can find, afford, and access quality care. That ambition sets us apart, and offers you an endless runway to impact one of the world's most urgent issues. We don’t have passenger seats here. Everyone is driving something that matters.

This work deserves real commitment. So if you thrive on meeting problems head on, untangling serious complexity, and working at pace with the sharpest yet kindest people around, you've come to the right place.

About the Internship

Where a day’s work is life-changing. Over 12 weeks, you’ll join a product engineering team and own a scoped project addressing a real client, provider, or business need. You’ll contribute to the technical approach and production code, work cross-functionally, and ship a solution with meaningful impact.

With support from a dedicated engineer Mentor and Engineering Manager, you’ll receive regular guidance, candid feedback, a midpoint review, and a final project review. As one of 10 interns in Grow’s founding New York City cohort, you’ll also participate in technical learning, leadership conversations, networking, and social experiences—and help shape the program for future interns.

What We Look for in an Intern

  • You’re building a strong technical foundation: You’re currently enrolled in a bachelor’s or master’s degree program in computer science, software engineering, or a related field, with an expected graduation date of Fall 2027 or Spring 2028. Through coursework or hands-on experience, you’ve developed familiarity with data structures, algorithms, software design, and at least one general-purpose programming language. Experience with Python, TypeScript, React, or similar technologies is helpful but not required.

  • You use AI tools with judgment: You’re comfortable using AI-assisted development tools to generate, debug, and verify code while thinking critically about correctness, privacy, security, and impact. (Claude, Cursor, Copilot, or similar)

  • You show potential through practice: You’ve applied your skills through projects, research, hackathons, open-source contributions, student organizations, an internship or co-op, or other hands-on experiences.

  • You bring a high bar and high care: You value quality and attention to detail while treating teammates with kindness, honesty, and respect.

  • You build for the people we serve: You stay close to client, provider, and health-plan needs and bring urgency to work that can improve access to mental healthcare.

What You'll Work On

  • Own a meaningful project that goes into production, becomes part of our product, and improves the client and provider experience.

  • Participate in planning, stand-ups, code reviews, demos, and retrospectives as a member of a product team

  • Investigate bugs, evaluate tradeoffs, and use data and customer context to improve your solution

  • Communicate progress, risks, decisions, and learnings throughout the internship

  • Present your project, technical approach, and impact at the end of the program

Program Details & Intern Benefits

  • Employment Type: Summer Internship, Full Time, Exempt

  • Program Dates: June 1–August 20, 2027 [12 weeks]

  • This is a hybrid role with the expectation to work onsite from our NYC hub location 3 days per week [Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday]

  • Base Compensation: $50/hr

  • Housing Stipend: $5,000

  • Meal Benefit [$25 per day DoorDash credit for onsite days]

  • Paid Company Holidays

Note: This is a temporary intern position, and as such, does not include benefits provided to full-time employees.

Full Time Employee Benefits:

  • Health Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life, and disability coverage.

  • Grow for Grow: No cost access to therapy through the Grow platform (available to US employees)

  • Financial Wellness: Retirement savings programs and equity opportunities to help you invest in your future.

  • Flexible Time Off, Paid Holidays & Winter Break: Flexible time off, company paid holidays (which vary by country), and a full company wide Winter Break to rest and recharge

  • Parental Leave: Up to 18 weeks of paid parental leave to support you and your growing family and a new child stipend.

  • Mental Health Mornings/Afternoons: Dedicated weekly flexible time for self care, whether that's therapy, exercise, journaling, time with family, or simply taking a break.

  • Wellness & Development Stipend: Annual stipend to support your personal wellbeing and professional growth, from fitness and education to books and learning resources.

  • Commuter Benefits: Pre tax commuter benefits to support teammates working from one of our hub locations.

  • Home Office & Meals: Support for your home workspace plus meal benefits, with offerings tailored to both remote and hub based employees.

  • Additional Perks: A variety of wellbeing benefits, including wellness memberships, virtual care, pet insurance discounts (where available), and global travel assistance.

We're seeking a Senior Manager to lead the teams responsible for Learning, Content, and Quality within our Shared Services organization. The role will work closely with broader Ops teams to build the connective tissue between their roadmap and what these leaders hope to accomplish. This role will own the planning, implementation, and continuous improvement for all three functions, which are at various stages of maturity.

What You’ll Do:

  • Directly manage, mentor, and develop teams in Training, Content, and Quality, creating clear career development paths and fostering a high-performing learning organization.

  • Develop and execute a multi-year strategic vision for support enablement that adapts to evolving business and scaling demands.

  • Assess the current maturity, operating model, team structure, and priorities across Learning, Content, and Quality Assurance, establishing a clear vision, roadmap, and the resources required to scale each function.

  • Overhaul and own the first-year onboarding journey, creating an engaging learning experience that minimizes frontline ramp time and reduces early-stage turnover.

  • Rebuild new-hire onboarding around a structured, measurable curriculum that enables trainers, not frontline Operations teams to own knowledge transfer, while using shadowing as reinforcement rather than the primary learning method.

  • Build the connective tissue with the Training, Content, and Quality Teams to build a closed-loop feedback system that identifies recurring frontline knowledge gaps and translates them into targeted content updates and learning solutions.

  • Design and implement a Train-the-Trainer framework to empower internal leaders and BPO vendor trainers to deliver high-quality instruction.

  • Own training performance metrics, including completion rates, assessment scores, 30/60/90-day performance, and the relationship between training outcomes and operational KPIs.

  • Create and enable the strategy for how AI can up-level each function, both at the individual function level and broadly across our Operations Department

  • Candidates need experience building structured onboarding and curriculum that reduces dependence on shadowing and Operations SMEs.

  • Own the strategy for assessing, building, and maintaining both internal and external knowledge bases.

You’ll Be a Good Fit If You Have:

  • 8+ years in support, operations, or a related function — with at least 3 years managing multiple teams or functions.

  • Experience leading or being a team member of Training, Content, and Quality in the past.

  • Comfortable in a start-up / fast-paced environment that requires a 0 -> 1 mindset

  • A transformative leader with a clear point of view on where AI-native support is headed and the drive to get there — you don't wait for the roadmap, you help write it.

  • Proficiency in tools like LMS (Learning Management Systems), CMS (Content Management Systems), Quality software, and other relevant software.

  • Strong people leadership and cross-functional communication skills, with the ability to create clarity in a new function, align operational and technical partners, and balance immediate needs with long-term reliability

Nice to Have

  • You have worked in healthcare, financial services, insurance, or another highly regulated environment.

Employment Type: Full Time, Exempt
Base Compensation: The base compensation range for this position is:

Fully Remote Commitment: $130,000 - $159,000 USD Annually

Hybrid Commitment: $155,000 - $190,000 USD Annually

This role can be hybrid (onsite from our NYC, San Francisco, or Seattle hub location three days per week: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday) or fully remote. Both arrangements include travel 2–3 times per year (e.g., company and department offsites).

The base compensation for this role will vary depending on several factors, including relevant experience, qualifications, and the candidate’s working location.

  • Health Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life, and disability coverage.

  • Mental Health Mornings/Afternoons: Dedicated weekly flexible time for self care, whether that's therapy, exercise, journaling, time with family, or simply taking a break.

Since launching in 2020, 15 million sessions have started on Grow, and we've barely scratched the surface. We do it through a three-sided marketplace that empowers providers, augments insurance payors, and serves patients. We've backed that ambition with more than $328M in funding, including our Series D at a $3B valuation from Sequoia Capital, Transformation Capital, TCV, SignalFire, Menlo Ventures, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, and others.

At Grow, the work you do can literally change someone's life. Your work here doesn't stay on a screen; it impacts whether someone can find, afford, and access quality care. That ambition sets us apart, and offers you an endless runway to impact one of the world's most urgent issues. We don’t have passenger seats here. Everyone is driving something that matters.

This work deserves real commitment. So if you thrive on meeting problems head on, untangling serious complexity, and working at pace with the sharpest yet kindest people around, you've come to the right place.

The Opportunity:
We are looking for an Growth Manager, Audio to help scale Grow's audio program — spanning podcast, streaming, and experimental audio placements — building on a foundation our team has already established. In this role, you'll own the channel end to end, accountable for both strategy and execution: managing a pipeline of host-read and run-of-network partnerships, and refining our mix of activation models. You'll manage vendor and partner relationships and negotiate new opportunities. And you'll continuously optimize toward efficiency and scale goals, all while building genuine brand affinity along the way.

You will work closely with our Director of Mass Media, Influencer Marketing Manager, Creative, Data, and leadership to shape channel strategy, bring creative direction to life in audio-specific formats, and grow this into one of Grow's most efficient and best-measured growth channels. You'll also own the roadmap that governs how we test new shows and partnerships against what's already working, and you'll be a driving voice in how we forecast and plan the channel's growth over time.

The ideal candidate is a seasoned audio or podcast marketer who is equal parts scrappy and strategic — someone with strong instincts for brand fit, experience negotiating and managing partner relationships, and a track record of building on and improving measurement and testing infrastructure. You're comfortable operating as a player-coach, executing the details of the channel while also stepping back to sharpen the roadmap that scales it. You bring rigor to how you read performance data, aren't afraid to challenge assumptions about what's working, and know how to make a case for a channel that doesn't have the clean, click-based attribution other channels enjoy.

What You'll Be Doing:

  • Own podcast/show pipeline management — sourcing sponsorships, ad placements, and vendor partnerships, and evaluating contextual alignment between shows and our target audience

  • Build a pipeline of new shows to test against established partnerships, and scale top-performing models

  • Refine our channel activation model — balancing and proving the value of host-read vs. run-of-network placements and sponsorships/partnerships

  • Own the audio channel roadmap, operationalizing a deliberate testing and scaling plan

  • Manage vendor/partner relationships end-to-end

  • Establish measurement methodology for a channel without clean click-based attribution (promo codes, vanity URLs, incrementality/lift testing) and manage day-to-day performance

  • Evaluate audio's halo effect on other channels as MMM infrastructure becomes available

  • Partner with the creative team on audio creative direction (input, not ownership)

This role is based in our New York, NY hub, where we require an in-office presence three days per week.

You'll Be a Good Fit If You Have:

  • You can take full ownership of a channel and are comfortable building testing frameworks and infrastructure from scratch

  • You have 5-7+ years managing paid media budgets, with direct audio/podcast buying experience (in-house DTC or healthcare background a plus)

  • You are analytically self-sufficient, and can use data tools to evaluate performance and communicate progress without hand-holding

  • You are comfortable managing external vendor/agency relationships and negotiating on Grow's behalf

  • You are extremely organized and can run a channel solo (player-coach) while still building toward how it scales

  • You have a strong point of view on measurement methodology in channels without clean attribution

Employment Type: Full Time, Exempt
Base Compensation: The base compensation range for this position is $144,000–$168,000 USD Annually


This is a hybrid role with the expectation to work onsite from our NYC, hub location three days per week (Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday) and travel 2–3 times per year (e.g., company and department offsites).
The base compensation for this role will vary depending on several factors, including relevant experience, qualifications, and the candidate’s working location.

Full Time Employee Benefits:

  • Health Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life, and disability coverage.

  • Grow for Grow: No cost access to therapy through the Grow platform (available to US employees)

  • Financial Wellness: Retirement savings programs and equity opportunities to help you invest in your future.

  • Flexible Time Off, Paid Holidays & Winter Break: Flexible time off, company paid holidays (which vary by country), and a full company wide Winter Break to rest and recharge

  • Parental Leave: Up to 18 weeks of paid parental leave to support you and your growing family and a new child stipend.

  • Mental Health Mornings/Afternoons: Dedicated weekly flexible time for self care, whether that's therapy, exercise, journaling, time with family, or simply taking a break.

  • Wellness & Development Stipend: Annual stipend to support your personal wellbeing and professional growth, from fitness and education to books and learning resources.

  • Commuter Benefits: Pre tax commuter benefits to support teammates working from one of our hub locations.

  • Home Office & Meals: Support for your home workspace plus meal benefits, with offerings tailored to both remote and hub based employees.

  • Additional Perks: A variety of wellbeing benefits, including wellness memberships, virtual care, pet insurance discounts (where available), and global travel assistance.

The Opportunity

We're looking for a performance marketer who wants to get their hands on the channels where most people first discover Grow. You'll sit on our paid media team focused on client acquisition, supporting day-to-day buying, analysis, and creative testing across paid social - Meta, TikTok, YouTube - plus creator and affiliate paid partnerships and a growing set of emerging channels. You'll report to our Performance Marketing Manager leading paid social.

This role is a blend of hands-on-keyboard media buying, real analytical work, and creative judgment. The best fit for this role questions assumptions and digs deeper when the numbers don't add up, rather than accepting surface-level explanations. You have a deep understanding of how paid social channels work and are motivated by the thought of helping us to build a best in class program. You balance attention to detail with a bias toward action - you ship experiments quickly, learn fast, and iterate. You're excited by the challenge of unlocking growth in competitive markets where the obvious tactics are saturated, and you're energized by mission-driven work.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Own day-to-day management and optimization of paid social campaigns - account structure, budgets, bidding, audiences, creative strategy (in partnership with growth and creative) and pacing against target

  • Build and run a high-velocity creative testing roadmap in partnership with our creative team: write the briefs, design the tests, read the results, and scale what works

  • Turn performance data into decisions - build your own reporting and analysis, identify lenses for channel measurement and evolve those over time, and bring recommendations

  • Support channel strategy and planning: forecasting, budget scenarios, marginal efficiency analysis, and weekly and monthly performance reporting

  • Help scale creator and affiliate paid partnerships: collaborating with agencies, sourcing and evaluating creators, briefing, and measuring performance (in close coordination with our influencer marketing lead and other growth/creative teammates)

  • Stand up and test emerging channels from proposal through launch and read, building the case for where we should place our next bets

  • Contribute to how we measure - incrementality and geo-lift testing, privacy-safe conversion tracking, and attribution in a channel mix where clean click-based attribution isn't always available

  • Partner cross-functionally with creative, data, conversion rate optimization, lifecycle, finance, and legal to improve the funnel end to end

  • Manage platform and vendor relationships day to day, holding partners accountable to what we need from them to reach our goals

You’ll Be a Good Fit If:

  • You have 3-5+ years in performance marketing with direct, hands-on paid social buying experience - you've been the person in ads manager, not just the person reading the report. Meta and TikTok experience is required; YouTube is strongly preferred

  • You've had experience scaling volume while managing to an efficiency target (CAC, ROAS, or LTV:CAC) for direct consumer acquisition, and you can talk about the specific decisions that moved core KPIs

  • You're analytically self-sufficient - you build your own pulls, you're fluent in spreadsheets and AI / BI tools (experience with Claude/Hex/Looker/Tableau is a plus), and you can take lead on both reading out test results and investigating when numbers don’t line up

  • You have strong creative instincts and a track record of briefing and iterating with creative partners. You can articulate and execute a testing framework

  • You take a structured, hypothesis-driven approach to performance, and you know how to isolate whether the issue is creative, audience, auction dynamics, landing experience, or measurement

  • You're extremely organized and comfortable prioritizing across a high volume of campaigns, tests, and partners

  • You have a point of view on how to measure channels where attribution is imperfect

  • Bonus points for:

    • Experience in healthcare or another regulated category with constrained tracking

    • Creator or affiliate paid partnership buying experience

    • Experience with incrementality or geo-lift testing, media mix modeling inputs, and/or an experimentation platform

    • App install acquisition experience with a mobile measurement partner

  • Mental Health Mornings/Afternoons: Dedicated weekly flexible time for self care, whether that's therapy, exercise, journaling, time with family, or simply taking a break.

  • Wellness & Development Stipend: Annual stipend to support your personal wellbeing and professional growth, from fitness and education to books and learning resources.

  • Commuter Benefits: Pre tax commuter benefits to support teammates working from one of our hub locations.

Since launching in 2020, 15 million sessions have started on Grow, and we've barely scratched the surface. We do it through a three-sided marketplace that empowers providers, augments insurance payors, and serves patients. Every solution we build reveals ten more waiting to be delivered, and that's just what gets us going. We've backed that ambition with more than $328M in funding, including our Series D at a $3B valuation from Sequoia Capital, Transformation Capital, TCV, SignalFire, Menlo Ventures, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, and others.

At Grow, the work you do can literally change someone's life. Your work here doesn't stay on a screen; it impacts whether someone can find, afford, and access quality care. That ambition sets us apart, and offers you an endless runway to impact one of the world's most urgent issues. We don’t have passenger seats here. Everyone is driving something that matters.

This work deserves real commitment. So if you thrive on meeting problems head on, untangling serious complexity, and working at pace with the sharpest yet kindest people around, you've come to the right place.

Grow Therapy is growing our Revenue Operations team, and we’re looking for a GTM Engineer to join the builders architecting the systems, data, and automation layer behind our commercial engine. This is a role built for range: you could be re-architecting the referral engine that turns physician outreach into inbound patient referrals for our Primary Care (PCP) motion, standing up a brand-new 0-to-1 system connecting benefits consultants, employers, and employees for our Employee Assistance Program (EAP), or building the recruitment, credentialing, and retention systems that let Grow recruit and retain the therapists and prescribers on our platform through Provider Experience. Every one of these is a real engineering problem, not a process-improvement exercise, and every one of them directly expands access to mental healthcare.

This is a high-ownership, builder-first role for someone who wants to work at the intersection of GTM strategy and hands-on systems engineering: architecting the data model, shipping the automation, and building the AI agents that let Grow’s commercial teams do more without growing headcount linearly. You’ll work in close partnership with the GTM Engineering Lead, Enterprise & GTM Architecture, who sets the standards for Grow’s GTM systems architecture end-to-end, and with the broader GTM Systems team as it takes shape.

A taste of the systems you could be building:

  • Primary Care (PCP): Design the data model and automation that convert physician-office outreach into a repeatable, inbound referral engine, and automate referral intake, validation, and routing.

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Map the end-to-end consultant → employer → employee journey and build the staging environment and data model from scratch to support a brand-new motion.

  • Provider Experience: Build the recruitment, credentialing, and retention pipeline that moves a provider from first application to an active, engaged member of Grow’s network.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Architect the system: Design and ship the end-to-end technical architecture for your assigned motion, spanning data model, automation logic, and integration patterns.

  • Build AI agents, not just workflows: Design and deploy AI agents (built on Claude) that autonomously perform GTM tasks (referral triage, document parsing, account research) rather than workflows that simply call an LLM API.

  • Run an experimentation loop: Treat new automations and agent behaviors as experiments: ship fast, measure impact, and iterate or kill based on data, not intuition.

  • Evolve the stack: Continuously evaluate the GTM tech stack (HubSpot, n8n/Workato, Segment, Gong, Aircall/Nooks, Clay) and recommend consolidation or upgrades as your motion matures and scales.

  • Sandbox everything: Implement rigorous testing and deployment so no logic goes live unvalidated.

  • Document the system: Maintain a technical schema map of your systems so the organization understands the logic behind every automation.

  • Own data governance: Define and enforce data governance standards (field definitions, ownership, quality rules, and access controls) for your data model as a core part of data strategy.

  • Build for resilience: Build monitoring and self-healing automations that alert the team when data syncs fail or logic breaks.

  • Align on shared architecture: Partner with the GTM Engineering Lead, Enterprise & GTM Architecture to apply consistent technical standards and governance practices across your systems and the rest of Grow’s GTM architecture.

Outcomes You’ll Own

Across PCP, EAP, and Provider Experience, the bar is the same: build systems that let volume grow without a proportional increase in manual effort. A few examples of what that looks like:

  • Grow the demand side (Primary Care): Increase the number and quality of inbound physician referrals and successful patient intakes.

  • Build the EAP foundation (EAP): Ship a 0-to-1 systems foundation robust enough to support Grow’s next phase of employer and consultant growth.

  • Maximize efficient supply (Provider Experience): Increase the number of credentialed, engaged therapists and prescribers Grow can support without a proportional increase in manual effort.

You’ll Be a Good Fit If You Have

  • Experience: 5+ years in a technical RevOps or GTM Engineering role; experience with healthcare, benefits, credentialing, or referral/recruiting systems is a plus.

  • An Architect Mindset: You see logic gates, data schemas, and API endpoints, and design for scale rather than one-off fixes.

  • HubSpot Mastery: Expert-level technical knowledge of HubSpot (Advanced Workflows, Custom Objects) as Grow’s core CRM.

  • Orchestration Fluency: Expert proficiency in n8n and Workato, and comfort integrating tools like Segment, Gong, Aircall, Nooks, and Clay, depending on your track.

  • AI Agent Builder: Proven experience building AI agents and agentic workflows (Claude, OpenAI, or Gemini) that autonomously perform GTM tasks, not just single-step LLM calls.

  • 0-to-1 & Multi-Stakeholder Comfort: Experience standing up net-new systems and data models for a channel or motion that didn’t previously exist, and/or designing CRM data models for complex, multi-party relationships.

  • Data Governance: Experience setting data governance standards (definitions, ownership, quality rules, access controls) as a core part of data strategy, not an afterthought bolted on once a model is live.

  • Lifecycle Thinking: Experience architecting systems that span both a funnel and an ongoing relationship, not just a single-stage pipeline.

Employment Type: Full Time, Exempt
Base Compensation: The base compensation range for this position is:

Hybrid Commitment: $114,000 - $133,000 USD Annually

This role will be hybrid (onsite from our NYC location three days per week: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday). The hybrid arrangement will include travel 2–3 times per year (e.g., company and department offsites).

Full Time Employee Benefits:

  • Health Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life, and disability coverage.

  • Grow for Grow: No cost access to therapy through the Grow platform (available to US employees)

  • Financial Wellness: Retirement savings programs and equity opportunities to help you invest in your future.

  • Flexible Time Off, Paid Holidays & Winter Break: Flexible time off, company paid holidays (which vary by country), and a full company wide Winter Break to rest and recharge

  • Parental Leave: Up to 18 weeks of paid parental leave to support you and your growing family and a new child stipend.

  • Mental Health Mornings/Afternoons: Dedicated weekly flexible time for self care, whether that's therapy, exercise, journaling, time with family, or simply taking a break.

  • Wellness & Development Stipend: Annual stipend to support your personal wellbeing and professional growth, from fitness and education to books and learning resources.

  • Commuter Benefits: Pre tax commuter benefits to support teammates working from one of our hub locations.

The Opportunity:

Grow Therapy's iOS app launched earlier this year, and mobile is now a core part of how clients find care, connect with their providers, and stay engaged between sessions. Android is next, and we're hiring our founding Android engineer to build it.

You'll report to our Director of Engineering for the Momentum pillar and work alongside the iOS, product, and design partners who built the first app.

This is a hands-on role in an AI-forward engineering organization. We expect the person in this seat to make deliberate architectural calls with incomplete information, ship the first release, and set the standards a growing Android team inherits.

What You'll Be Doing:

  • Design the architecture and technical foundations for Grow's native Android app, from project structure and state management through build, testing, and release infrastructure.

  • Ship consumer-facing features on that foundation, building the experiences that help clients discover care, connect with providers, and manage their care journey between sessions.

  • Set coding standards, tooling, and engineering practices for Android, and evolve them as the team grows around you.

  • Own the path to production: CI/CD, Google Play release management, observability, and the quality and security practices a healthcare app requires.

  • Partner closely with product, design, and the iOS and backend teams to connect technical decisions to product goals, and product goals back to technical tradeoffs.

  • Drive cross-functional decisions and represent Android's roadmap and tradeoffs to stakeholders across the company, often without a precedent to point to.

You'll Be a Good Fit If:

  • You have 8+ years of software engineering experience, the majority in native Android development with Kotlin, spanning both platform/architecture work and consumer-facing feature development.

  • You have led the technical direction for an Android app or platform from an early or 0-to-1 stage, or through a major re-architecture: you chose the architecture, stood up the tooling, shipped to production, and are comfortable making those calls with incomplete information and no established playbook.

  • You have production depth in modern Android: Jetpack Compose, Kotlin coroutines and Flow, dependency injection, modularization, and Gradle build tooling, and a considered testing strategy.

  • You have strong product instincts and a genuine ability to partner with product and design, connecting technical decisions to what users actually experience.

  • You use AI development tools (e.g., Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) as a core part of how you build, and have grounded opinions on where they help and where they don't.

Bonus:

  • You have a personal connection to mental health care or a strong pull toward Grow's mission.

  • You have a considered view on Kotlin Multiplatform and shared-code strategies, grounded in something you've shipped or evaluated.

  • You've built mobile apps in a regulated or healthcare setting, with real attention to sensitive data and accessibility.

  • You've helped uplevel an Android team around you through hiring, mentoring, and standards others adopted.

 - Design the architecture and technical foundations for Grow's native Android app, from project structure and state management through build, testing, and release infrastructure.

 - Ship consumer-facing features on that foundation, building the experiences that help clients discover care, connect with providers, and manage their care journey between sessions.

 - Set coding standards, tooling, and engineering practices for Android, and evolve them as the team grows around you.

 - Own the path to production: CI/CD, Google Play release management, observability, and the quality and security practices a healthcare app requires.

 - Partner closely with product, design, and the iOS and backend teams to connect technical decisions to product goals, and product goals back to technical tradeoffs.

 - Drive cross-functional decisions and represent Android's roadmap and tradeoffs to stakeholders across the company, often without a precedent to point to.



You'll Be a Good Fit If:

 - You have 8+ years of software engineering experience, the majority in native Android development with Kotlin, spanning both platform/architecture work and consumer-facing feature development.

 - You have led the technical direction for an Android app or platform from an early or 0-to-1 stage, or through a major re-architecture: you chose the architecture, stood up the tooling, shipped to production, and are comfortable making those calls with incomplete information and no established playbook.

 - You have production depth in modern Android: Jetpack Compose, Kotlin coroutines and Flow, dependency injection, modularization, and Gradle build tooling, and a considered testing strategy.

 - You have strong product instincts and a genuine ability to partner with product and design, connecting technical decisions to what users actually experience.

 - You use AI development tools (e.g., Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) as a core part of how you build, and have grounded opinions on where they help and where they don't.



Bonus:

 - You have a personal connection to mental health care or a strong pull toward Grow's mission.

 - You have a considered view on Kotlin Multiplatform and shared-code strategies, grounded in something you've shipped or evaluated.

 - You've built mobile apps in a regulated or healthcare setting, with real attention to sensitive data and accessibility.

 - You've helped uplevel an Android team around you through hiring, mentoring, and standards others adopted.
